memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Completed." After chapters of instructions, offerings, weaving, casting and carving, the work was finished.

The wording deliberately echoes the creation account, where God finished His work and saw that it was very good (Gen 1:31; 2:1-2). A new dwelling place had been made, and God's people had built it exactly as told.

Take a moment to appreciate what this represents. These were former slaves who, not long before, had melted their jewellery into a calf. Now they had completed an intricate, beautiful sanctuary in the desert without deviating from God's design.

Grace does more than forgive. It restores and produces obedience.

Notice the emphasis: "just as the Lord commanded Moses." Not their best interpretation. Not an improved version. Obedience is the theme of this whole chapter — the phrase appears repeatedly, almost insistently.

There is one greater completion still. On the cross, Jesus said, "It is finished" (John 19:30). Israel completed a tent; Christ completed our redemption. Their work made a dwelling place possible; His work makes us the dwelling place (Eph 2:22).

And He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God brought to completion in your life that once seemed impossible?
2. Where are you tempted to improve on God's instructions rather than follow them?
3. What unfinished work is God asking you to persevere with?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You finish what You begin. Give me grace to obey exactly, not approximately. Amen.
